q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is scheduled for Wednesday, August 26, 2026. Today is August 22, 2026. This means resolution occurs in **4 days**.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** (not actual results) for Q2 FY2027 revenue. According to the research provided, NVIDIA has already issued this guidance:

**NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%**, which implies a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion.

This guidance was provided when they announced Q1 FY2027 results. The earnings release on August 26, 2026 will either:
1. Reaffirm this $91.0 billion guidance, or
2. Raise or lower the guidance based on updated business trends

Given that:
- The guidance was just issued (with Q1 results)
- Only ~4 days pass before the next earnings call
- NVIDIA's business momentum appears strong (85% YoY growth in Q1)
- The range of $89.2B-$92.8B provides a reasonable buffer
- Wall Street's average estimate of $91.9B falls comfortably within the guided range

The most likely scenario is that NVIDIA **reaffirms or slightly adjusts** the $91.0 billion guidance, keeping it in the $89.2B-$92.8B range.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Significant deterioration in near-term demand signals in the 4 days since Q1 results
- Unexpected supply chain disruptions
- Geopolitical escalation affecting China revenue restrictions (though already assumed at zero)
- Material customer order cancellations or deferrals
- Competitive pressure from AMD or other entrants materializing faster than expected

These scenarios seem unlikely given the tight timeframe and strong momentum indicated.

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Better-than-expected demand signals in H100/H200 ramps
- Accelerated AI adoption driving pull-forward of orders
- Expanded customer base beyond the major hyperscalers
- Upside surprise in non-Data Center segments (Gaming, Professional Visualization, Automotive)
- Management confidence warranting modest upward revision

Given NVIDIA's recent strong execution and analyst expectations at $91.9B (above the midpoint), modest upside seems more likely than downside.

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research explicitly provides NVIDIA's own forward guidance: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** ($89.2B-$92.8B). This is the most reliable "base rate" for this forecast, as it represents NVIDIA management's own projection issued just before this earnings call.

Historical context from the research:
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6B
- Sequential growth in Q1: 20%
- Guidance represents ~11.6% sequential growth Q1→Q2

---

## Probability Distribution

Given that:
1. NVIDIA has already provided explicit forward guidance of $91.0B ± 2%
2. The company has strong momentum and execution
3. Analyst consensus ($91.9B) sits comfortably within the guided range
4. Only 4 days remain, limiting major new information
5. The ± 2% range provides a reasonable buffer

The most likely outcome is reaffirmation of the $91.0B guidance or a minor adjustment within the $89.2B-$92.8B range.

I model the distribution as:
- 60% probability the guidance remains at $91.0B (reaffirmed)
- 25% probability modest upward revision to ~$92.0B
- 10% probability guidance stays within guided range but mid-point shifts slightly
- 5% probability of larger moves outside stated range

Low (10th percentile): 89200000000
Median (50th percentile): 91000000000
High (90th percentile): 92800000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, after the close of trading [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8).

For Q1 FY2027 (ended April 26, 2026), NVIDIA reported record revenue of \$81.6 billion, an 85% increase year-over-year and 20% sequentially [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). Data Center revenue reached \$75.2 billion, up 92% from a year ago [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).

NVIDIA's guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue is \$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, implying a range of \$89.2 billion to \$92.8 billion [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around \$91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which falls within NVIDIA's projected range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
